question: Which of the following statements about combinatorial testing are correct?

options.text: It focuses on designing test cases based on combinations of input parameter values
Pairwise testing is a form of combinatorial testing
It guarantees exhaustive testing of all program paths
It helps reduce the number of test cases while still detecting many faults
It is mainly used only for white-box testing

solution: Combinatorial testing designs test cases using combinations of input values. Pairwise testing is a common form that reduces test cases while still detecting many faults.

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: In combinatorial testing, a “t-way interaction” refers to:

options.text: Testing interactions among t input parameters
Executing t program statements simultaneously
Testing only t test cases
Ensuring every combination of any t parameter values appears at least once
Measuring test execution time for t seconds

solution: A t-way interaction means interactions among any 𝑡input parameters are tested, ensuring every combination of those 𝑡parameter values appears at least once.

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: Consider a system with three Boolean input parameters A, B, and C. Which of the following statements are true regarding exhaustive combinational testing?

options.text: Exhaustive combinatorial testing would require 16 test cases
Pairwise testing would always require 8 test cases
Exhaustive testing checks every possible input combination
Combinatorial testing can sometimes reduce the number of test cases
Decision tables are typically used to design exhaustive combinatorial testing

solution: Exhaustive combinatorial testing checks all possible input combinations. Combinatorial techniques like pairwise testing can reduce the number of required test cases.

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: A railway ticket booking system is to be tested using a decision table with the following conditions: Seats available, Payment successful, Passenger verified. The actions include: Confirm booking, Generate waiting ticket, Ask to retry payment, Reject booking. Which of the following statements are true?

options.text: A rule would be if payment fails, ask to retry payment action is triggered
“Confirm booking” action would require all conditions to be satisfied
Decision tables help systematically derive minimal test cases for exhaustive testing
Exhaustive program path testing is ensured when using decision table-based testing
Multiple rules in a decision table can map to the same action

solution: Decision tables map condition combinations to actions. Multiple rules may lead to the same action, and confirming booking requires all necessary conditions to be satisfied

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: In cause-effect graphing, which of the following are correctly matched?

options.text: Causes → Input conditions
Effects → Output conditions
Nodes → Representation of causes and effects
Constraints → Restrictions on outputs only
Intermediate nodes → Randomly generated test cases

solution: Causes represent input conditions, effects represent output conditions, and nodes represent causes/effects in the graph. Constraints are not restrictions on outputs only, and intermediate nodes represent logical expressions, not test cases.

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: Which of the following statements about black-box testing are true?

options.text: It guarantees complete statement coverage
It is impossible to test every possible input-output combination for non-trivial systems
Some parts of the code may remain unreachable during testing
It can determine whether extra functionality has been implemented
It focuses on functional behavior without examining internal code

solution: Black-box testing focuses only on external behavior and cannot ensure complete code coverage. Some code may remain unexecuted during testing.

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: Which of the following are true regarding the shortcomings of relying on only one testing approach?

options.text: Using only black-box testing may leave some code untested
Using only white-box testing may fail to detect missing requirements
White-box testing is preferred as it guarantees functional correctness
Black-box testing is preferred as it guarantees detection of extra functionality
Both approaches together provide complete fault detection

solution: Only black-box testing may leave some internal code untested, while only white-box testing may miss missing or incorrect requirements.

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: For the following program statement, which of the following test suites would achieve basic condition coverage?
solution: Basic condition coverage requires each atomic condition (x>=5 and y<20) to evaluate to both True and False at least once across the test suite. Options (a), (d), and (e) satisfy this requirement.

topic: White-Box Testing, Control Flow Graphs & Condition Coverage
question: At least how many test cases are needed for achieving decision coverage on the given C code?
solution: Decision coverage requires each decision to evaluate to both True and False at least once. Two test cases are sufficient to cover all outcomes of both if statements

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: Which of the following statements regarding cyclomatic complexity are true?

options.text: Higher cyclomatic complexity for a code indicates higher code quality
Higher cyclomatic complexity may indicate more potential errors in code
Cyclomatic complexity correlates well with execution speed directly
Programs with higher complexity may require more effort to understand
Cyclomatic complexity can be related to the effort required for debugging

solution: Higher cyclomatic complexity usually indicates more complex code, which may increase error probability, understanding difficulty, and debugging effort

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: Which of the following are true regarding the coverage strength of various white-box testing techniques?

options.text: Statement coverage is among the weakest criteria shown
All path coverage is among the strongest criteria shown
Branch coverage guarantees multiple-condition coverage
MC/DC is stronger than branch and condition coverage
Condition coverage alone guarantees branch coverage

solution: Statement coverage is relatively weak, while all path coverage is very strong. MC/DC is stronger than branch and condition coverage because it checks independent effect of each condition.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: Which of the following statements about basis path coverage are true?

options.text: It is also known as all path coverage
It is stronger than statement coverage
It guarantees exhaustive testing of all possible paths
It is related to cyclomatic complexity
It is weaker than branch coverage

solution: Basis path coverage tests independent execution paths and is stronger than statement coverage. It is directly related to cyclomatic complexity.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: Which of the following statements regarding data flow testing are true?

options.text: It focuses on the definition and use of variables in a program
It is a fault-based testing technique
It ignores control flow in the program completely
It helps detect anomalies such as variables being used before initialization
It is based on tracking the life cycle of data objects

solution: Data flow testing analyzes variable definitions and uses to detect anomalies like using variables before initialization by tracking the data life cycle.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: Which of the following statements regarding mutation testing are true?

options.text: Equivalent mutants indicate that additional or improved test cases may be needed
Mutants are created by introducing small changes into the program
A mutant is said to be “killed” if a test case fails due to the change
Mutation testing is primarily a black-box testing technique
Mutation testing helps evaluate the effectiveness of a test suite

solution: Mutation testing creates small code changes called mutants. A mutant is “killed” when test cases detect the change, helping evaluate test suite effectiveness.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: Which of the following are objectives of mutation testing?

options.text: Assess the fault-detection capability of test cases
Improve the quality of the test suite
Guarantee absence of all software defects
Identify weak test cases and eliminate them from the test suite
Identify duplicate and equivalent test cases and optimize the test suite

solution: Mutation testing evaluates how effectively test cases detect faults and helps improve the quality of the test suite.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: In the context of mutation testing, suppose in a C program, the statement if(a > b) c=0; is replaced by if(a>=b-1) c=0; What kind of mutant has most likely been created?

options.text: Trivial mutant
Stillborn mutant
Higher-order mutant
Equivalent mutant
Syntax mutant

solution: The modified condition behaves similarly to the original for many integer values, so the mutant may produce the same output as the original program.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: What would be the Cyclomatic complexity measure of the following program?
solution: There are 3 if conditions, so complexity = 𝟑 + 𝟏 = 𝟒.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
question: Which of the following are major challenges associated with mutation testing?

options.text: Mutation testing improves the fault-detection capability of test cases
Generating and managing mutants needs to be done manually, thereby resulting in a dramatic increase in testing costs
Large numbers of mutants may need to be executed
Equivalent mutants are difficult to identify automatically
Mutation testing is not as effective as other testing techniques

solution: Mutation testing may require executing many mutants, and equivalent mutants are difficult to detect automatically, making the process expensive and complex.

topic: Path Coverage, Cyclomatic Complexity & Mutation Testing
